overview: Both are made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary, but they act on completely different target tissues.
genZNote: ADH: keeps your body from losing too much water. Oxytocin: the 'labour and bonding' hormone.

aspects.label: Main Trigger for Release
aspects.valueA: Increased blood osmolarity (dehydration) or decreased blood volume.
aspects.valueB: Cervical stretching during childbirth, or suckling during breastfeeding.

aspects.label: Also Called
aspects.valueB: Sometimes called the 'love hormone' for its role in bonding.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both ADH and oxytocin are synthesised by the hypothalamus and only stored/released by the posterior pituitary — a favourite exam trap.
overlay.memoryTrick: ADH = anti-diuretic, saves water. Oxytocin = labour contractions and milk let-down.
overlay.commonMisconception: ADH deficiency causes diabetes insipidus, not diabetes mellitus — a commonly confused pair of similarly-named conditions.
